[GRADED — Prelab 2 — Warehouse Inventory Report] Write a C program that prepares a warehouse inventory report.

Read four positive integer values from user input on the same line, separated by spaces, in the following order:
  • the number of items in each carton (itemsPerCarton)
  • the number of cartons (cartonCount)
  • the number of items that must be reserved (reservedItems)
  • the number of workers who will share the remaining items (workerCount)

Use these variable names or similarly meaningful names. You may use either camel case or underscores consistently. Assume the worker count is not zero and that the number of reserved items does not exceed the total inventory.

Print the following:
  • All four original input values.
  • The total inventory, calculated as items per carton times the number of cartons.
  • The number of items available after the reserved items are removed.
  • The integer number of available items each worker receives.
  • The number of available items left over after dividing among the workers.
  • A check value: items per worker times worker count, plus the leftover items. This should equal the number of available items.
  • Use TWO SEPARATE if statements to print an inventory decision:
      – If leftover items equals zero, print that the items divide evenly among the workers.
      – If leftover items is greater than zero, print that some items remain after the workers receive equal shares.

Sample Output 1:
Enter items/carton, cartons, reserved items, and workers: 24 15 38 7

*** Inventory values ***
Items per carton = 24
Number of cartons = 15
Reserved items = 38
Number of workers = 7

*** Inventory calculations ***
Total inventory = 360
Items available for workers = 322
Items per worker = 46
Items left over = 0
Check: distributed plus leftover = 322

*** Inventory decision ***
The items divide evenly among the workers.

Sample Output 2:
Enter items/carton, cartons, reserved items, and workers: 18 9 25 8

*** Inventory values ***
Items per carton = 18
Number of cartons = 9
Reserved items = 25
Number of workers = 8

*** Inventory calculations ***
Total inventory = 162
Items available for workers = 137
Items per worker = 17
Items left over = 1
Check: distributed plus leftover = 137

*** Inventory decision ***
Some items remain after the workers receive equal shares.
